newsitem.title: USA: Moderate House Democrats form group.
newsitem.headline: Moderate House Democrats form group.

text.p: A group of 32 House Democrats Thursday formed the New Democratic Coalition to encourage more moderate policies for their party.

"We believe that the future of the Democrat party depends upon the advancement of a moderate, pro-growth agenda that rejects the politics and the policies of the past and embraces new approaches -- both economic and social -- for our future," said Representative Cal Dooley of California, one the group's founders.
Representative Tim Roemer of Indiana said the group believed in fiscal constraint, a smaller, more efficient government and programmes to improve education and protect the environment.

"The big lesson of the last two years is that Democrats and Republicans need to tone down their rhetoric and focus more closely on solving the nation's problems in a civil and constructive manner," added Representative James Moran of Virginia.
A similar group, the Democratic Leadership Council, includes several moderate Democratic senators such as Charles Robb of Virginia, John Bureaux of Louisiana and former Georgia Sen. Sam Nunn.
